reads_as_reason: Block head with a square visor, shoulder boxes far wider than the references, and straight-sided untapered limbs and torso still read as a character or toy robot. The A10 two-tone tidy-up helps only slightly.

G1.evidence: Head is a rounded cube with a rectangular visor window (two-tone front view). Chest is a flat-fronted box with a ledge where the shoulder blocks sit. Arms splay out in a wide A. In the equal-height lineup the front silhouette is clearly broader than optimus_like and atlas_like, with no waist and no taper. Metrics agree: P3 shoulder width 0.412 vs band 0.22-0.29, P8a/P8b/P9b taper failures.

G2.evidence: Chest, waist and pelvis are separate stacked blocks. The chest box and pelvis box have a horizontal step between them, and the waist band reads as a stripe, not a flowing neck-to-hip form. Thighs and shanks are near-parallel columns, so the leg has no flowing taper. The side view shows a large rectangular pack and pelvis block hanging off the back, with a notch above the knee. Joints are straight dark horizontal bands, not recesses that the shells flow into.

G3.evidence: Two-tone view uses matte warm-white shells, graphite bands and a glossy black visor, with no accent colour. In A10 the bands are clean horizontal bands with sharp edges. Remaining flaws are the black heel box against white feet and a very heavy black shoulder and chest area in the side view.

G4.evidence: Head, chest, shoulder boxes and the rear heel block are tight-radius boxes. Thighs, shanks and forearms are soft capsules with large radii. The foot is a flat slab. Section squareness is not shared across segments, so the parts do not look like one family of primitives.

G6.evidence: Matches: head sits at the same height and the leg and knee landmarks roughly line up (P6 and P7 pass). Does not match: shoulders and arms are much wider and splayed, there is no waist taper, no neck column, feet are long slabs (P10a 0.238), and legs do not taper. S2 IoU is 0.53 vs optimus_like and 0.56 vs atlas_like, consistent with the visual mismatch.

pairwise.evidence: The two silhouettes are almost identical and both read as a toy. Candidate (Image A) is slightly better. Its two-tone knee, ankle and wrist bands are clean and continuous, where the baseline (Image B) has ragged black blotches at the knee in the side and back views and at the heel and shin. The shoulder and neck metrics are marginally closer to the band (P3 0.412 vs 0.418, S3 ledge count 4 vs 5, ledge total 0.884 vs 1.288). The difference is small and does not change the toy reading.

top_changes.change: Narrow the shoulders and arms by a large amount, close to the reference outline (about 0.41 H down toward the 0.22-0.29 band). Move the shoulder balls inboard, tuck the arms closer to the torso, and slim the upper arm. This is the biggest cause of the oversized, toy-like top half.

Make chest, waist and pelvis one continuous form. Taper the chest into a visibly narrower waist (waist/shoulder currently only just inside the band), then flare to the pelvis with no flat step. Give thighs and shanks a real taper: wide at the top, narrow at the knee and ankle, with the calf widest near the top third.
top_changes.profile_param: segments[torso].stations[waist].w / d; segments[thigh].stations[distal].w; segments[shank].stations[ankle].w and stations[calf].z

top_changes.change: Raise the radii and lower the squareness (n) of the head, chest and shoulder blocks to match the leg capsules. Round the head into a smoother egg or capsule and shorten the foot slab (P10a 0.238 vs band 0.13-0.17). Lengthen the neck slightly (P2a 0.1176 vs band 0.18-0.55). Fold the heel block into the shank or foot.

notes: Only the rendered views were used. The shaded studio views are flat, so subtle surface curvature is hard to judge. Numbers are quoted from design_metrics.json as given. The picture does not contradict any metric. The back view of the pelvis shows two odd rectangular thigh-top blocks that I could not identify from the images. I could not judge whether the dark bands are real recesses or only recolouring. Panel lines and surface detail are out of scope for step D1.
